entities.summary:
Aigan was a Hun general who served as a cavalry commander for the Byzantine Empire, active in the early 6th century. He played a crucial role in several military campaigns against the Sassanid Empire, utilizing tactics that would later become standard in the Byzantine military. Aigan's military successes were largely due to his skill in adapting Hunnic cavalry tactics to the Byzantine army's needs, demonstrating the importance of military innovation in shaping the course of history.

Aigan's legacy extends to his influence on the development of the Byzantine cavalry, which would go on to play a significant role in the empire's military successes for centuries to come. His military campaigns also contributed to the Byzantine Empire's ongoing struggle against the Sassanid Empire, setting the stage for the complex web of alliances and rivalries that defined the ancient Near East.

The Byzantine Empire's continued reliance on Hunnic cavalry tactics is a testament to Aigan's lasting impact on the military strategies of the empire. His military campaigns and the tactics he employed would be studied and emulated by military leaders for centuries to come, solidifying his place in the annals of military history.

Aigan's story is a reminder that even the most seemingly minor figures can have a profound impact on the course of human history. His bravery, strategic thinking, and adaptability in the face of overwhelming odds make him a fascinating figure in the history of the Byzantine Empire.
